Hi Anna / Tom / Medix security team —

Thanks for the patience. Attached are three items you requested: 1) processing-territories-matrix.xlsx (one-page matrix), 2) subprocessor-inventory.csv (service / country / region / persistence), and 3) SOC2-attestation.pdf. Key points and narrative below.

Executive summary
- Hosted API: primary processing occurs in the region selected at account creation. Default: US East (us-east-1). EU-region option (eu-west-1) is available by request and will keep inference and embeddings processing within EU data centers.
- Subprocessors: primary cloud provider is Amazon Web Services (hosting) with physical locations in us-east-1 and eu-west-1. Logging/observability is handled by CloudSecure (US/EU), and metrics/telemetry are processed by MetricFlow (US). The attached CSV maps each subprocessor to the region(s) where they process customer data.
- Cross-border transfers: for hosted customers who opt into EU-region processing, inference and embeddings remain in eu-west-1. Global orchestration metadata and some operational telemetry may traverse to redwood-managed services in the US for processing; we mark telemetry as pseudonymized and retain it for service health only. We do not replicate customer inference data to other regions unless explicitly configured in the customer's account settings.
- Retention and deletion:
  - API input (prompts): default retention 30 days for abuse and quality monitoring; can be shortened by contract for enterprise customers.
  - Ephemeral KV cache: stored in-region and expires by default after 24 hours; not persisted to backups.
  - Embeddings: stored per-customer configuration; default: 0 days unless customer enables embedding storage.
  - Deletion SLA: for hosted accounts, we remove data from active stores within 72 hours of a verified deletion request; trace records/operational logs that reference request metadata may persist longer for audit and billing purposes (standard retention window is 180 days). Private deployments follow customer-managed retention by default.

Evidence and next steps
- SOC2: attached attestation (latest).
- DPA: link to the redwood DPA is included above; we can share an executed DPA template and highlight any negotiated clause language.
- If Medix requires strict EU-only processing for all telemetry and orchestration, we recommend Dedicated or Private deployment models; we can propose a runbook and timeline.

Please see the attached matrix and inventory for row-level detail. If you'd like, we can hop on a 30-minute call to walk through the CSV and point to exact subprocessor regions.

Next steps I propose:
- Confirm whether you need: EU-only (no US telemetry) or just EU processing for inference/embeddings.
- If EU-only: I'll coordinate with Product on Dedicated options and timeline.
- If the matrix is good, confirm and I'll route the DPA and SOC2 paperwork through legal.

Best regards,
